b6d8f9da3047891c179408bf937652d24d430b40.summary: IBM X-Force researchers report that Zeus Sphinx, a commercially sold banking Trojan that emerged in August 2015 against UK banks, has been found in Brazil. The Brazilian variant, Sphinx v2, targets online banking and Boleto payment services at three top Brazilian banks and one Colombian bank. It uses real-time webinjections to collect PINs and personal data, and can reroute Boleto payments to the criminal by generating altered barcodes. The malware is sold on underground forums. b61e4c6ba0bf6f9658599075cdee2c82a340f909.summary: Ransom-ISAC, working with Bridewell, analysed command-and-control infrastructure from an intrusion. The intrusion began as an apparent phishing campaign using a private GitHub repository and aimed at developers, with cryptocurrency and data theft as the goal. Infrastructure was clustered by hosting provider, server fingerprint and RDP certificate. Cluster overlap with Aikido's reporting on an npm supply-chain campaign is assessed with moderate to high confidence. Ransom-ISAC assesses with low to medium confidence that two threat actors work together, with a possible DPRK link and…
